sehemu: Part II: Members of Parliament, Constituencies and Election of Members
maudhui: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Article, the United Republic shall be divided into constituencies in such number and manner as the Electoral Commission shall determine with the approval of the President. (2) Subject to any law applicable in that behalf, the Electoral Commission shall, with the approval of the President, have power to demarcate constituency boundaries. (3) In demarcating constituency boundaries, the Electoral Commission shall have due regard to the availability of means of communication and the geographical conditions of the area intended to be divided into constituencies. (4) Subject to this Constitution and any law relating to the division of the country into constituencies, the Electoral Commission may from time to time, and at least once every ten years, review the division of the United Republic into constituencies and may alter constituencies as a result of that review or of a population census of the United Republic. (5) Where, following a review of the division of the United Republic into constituencies, changes are made in constituency boundaries, the number of Members representing constituencies, the number of constituencies or the number of Members, any resulting change in the number of Members representing constituencies shall take effect upon the next dissolution of Parliament after such change. (6) Notwithstanding the other provisions of this Article, no court shall have jurisdiction to inquire into anything done by the Commission in the exercise of its function of dividing the United Republic into constituencies.

(6) Notwithstanding the other provisions of this Article, no court shall have jurisdiction to inquire into anything done by the Commission in the exercise of its function of dividing the United Republic into constituencies.
